pill.desc: pale yellow, round, film-coated, biconvex tablet

clues.kinetics: Food raises exposure, with meals increasing AUC by 33% to 66%. It is highly bound, at least 98.9%, to plasma protein, and feces carry 53% of the dose unchanged.
clues.substance: A sodium salt that is slightly soluble in water; the free acid has a molecular weight of 419.4.
clues.product: Approved under an NDA as 10, 25 and 50 mg tablets, dosed once daily, with a dispersible tablet for oral suspension.
clues.safety: With no boxed warning, it is contraindicated after prior hypersensitivity and with dofetilide. Insomnia, fatigue and headache are the most common reactions.
clues.indication: HIV-1 infection in adults and pediatric patients weighing at least 2 kg, combined with other antiretrovirals, or with rilpivirine as a complete regimen.
clues.mechanism: An HIV integrase strand transfer inhibitor, an antiretroviral agent that acts against HIV-1.

tell: A 14-hour terminal half-life, and a meal that lifts exposure by up to 66%, set this integrase inhibitor apart.

evidence.pk.tmaxH: peak plasma concentrations were observed 1 to 3 hours postdose
